429	## D-020 — Inventory costing (moving average + FIFO layers, same-transaction COGS, no negative stock)
430	
431	**Decision.**
432	`inv_items.costing_method` enum MOVING_AVERAGE|FIFO, defaulted from item category, changeable only while no stock exists. Quantity SSOT remains `inv_stock_moves`.
433	
434	**Moving average:** `inv_item_valuations` (tenant_id, item_id, warehouse_id, on_hand_qty QuantityType, avg_unit_cost full-precision, total_value MoneyType; UNIQUE(tenant_id, item_id, warehouse_id)), updated in the SAME transaction as the move under `select(...).with_for_update()` — on Postgres this takes the row lock serializing concurrent movers; on SQLite the dialect silently OMITS the FOR UPDATE clause (it is a no-op, not an error — clarified from the drafts' contradictory claims), and SQLite's single-writer lock provides equivalent serialization; the PG locking path is proven by pg-marked concurrency tests in CI.
435	- Receipt: `total_value += receipt_value; on_hand_qty += qty; avg_unit_cost = total_value / on_hand_qty` unrounded.
436	- Issue: `cogs = quantize(qty × avg_unit_cost, currency dp, HALF_UP); total_value -= cogs`; when on_hand_qty hits 0, residual total_value is flushed to the price-difference account so value and quantity never disagree.
437	
438	**FIFO:** `inv_cost_layers` (id, tenant_id, item_id, warehouse_id, receipt_move_id FK, received_at, original_qty, remaining_qty with CHECK `remaining_qty >= 0 AND remaining_qty <= original_qty`, unit_cost) plus `inv_layer_consumptions` (issue_move_id, layer_id, qty, cost). Issues consume layers ordered (received_at, id) ascending under `with_for_update`, one consumption row per touched layer; COGS = sum of per-layer quantized qty × unit_cost. Reversing an issue replays consumption rows backwards onto the exact layers; vendor returns consume layers normally; customer returns create a new layer at original COGS cost.
439	
440	**COGS consistency:** the in-process bus dispatches synchronously in the SAME session/transaction — inventory writes move + valuation/layer updates, publishes `inventory.stock.issued` carrying the computed cost and dimensions; `finance/handlers.py` posts the COGS journal entry (Dr COGS / Cr Inventory, dimensions copied: item, warehouse, cost center/WBS) before commit. One commit = move + valuation + journal + docflow link; a stock move can never exist without its journal entry or vice versa — explicitly recorded as the v1 decision whose future Kafka swap introduces a transactional outbox then, not now.
441	
442	**Negative stock forbidden outright:** service raises InsufficientStockError pre-flight, DB CHECKs (`on_hand_qty >= 0`, `remaining_qty >= 0`) back it; no per-warehouse opt-in. **Deadlock avoidance:** any transaction touching multiple valuation rows locks in (item_id, warehouse_id) sort order.
443	
444	**Rationale.**
445	The parity doc commits to moving average AND FIFO per item category with event-driven COGS posting. Same-transaction handling is the only design keeping stock value in the journal identical to the valuation table without reconciliation machinery, while the bus abstraction still decouples the modules at code level per CLAUDE.md rule 6. Layer consumption rows make COGS auditable per layer and reversals exact rather than recomputed. Banning negative stock makes FIFO well-defined and keeps the valuation CHECKs simple; shortage handling belongs to ATP/backorders per the parity doc.
446	
447	**Rejected alternatives.**
448	- Async/after-commit COGS: opens a stock-vs-GL divergence window requiring reconciliation jobs that contradict the universal-journal philosophy.
449	- Negative stock with provisional cost and retroactive correction (Odoo-style): requires retroactive revaluation clashing with posted-entry immutability.
450	- Global valuation row without warehouse dimension: parity scope is multi-warehouse and transfers need per-warehouse value.
451	- Report-time FIFO COGS recomputation: COGS must be a posted journal fact or statements change as layers mutate.
452	
453	**Risks & mitigations.**
454	- A finance handler bug rolls back inventory operations — intended (correctness over availability), documented for operators, tightly tested on the handler path.
455	- Moving-average rounding drift — absorbed by the zero-quantity flush rule, tested explicitly.
456	- SQLite cannot exercise true lock contention — accepted; the pg-marked tests carry that burden in CI.
457	
458	---
459	
460	## D-021 — Statements as pure projections + account-type model
461	
462	**Decision.**
463	`fin_accounts` (tenant_id, code, name, account_type ASSET|LIABILITY|EQUITY|REVENUE|EXPENSE, normal_balance derived from type, is_postable, cash_flow_category nullable OPERATING|INVESTING|FINANCING, is_cash_equivalent, account_group_id FK); `fin_account_groups` (tenant_id, code, name, parent_id self-FK, sort_order) as a pure presentation hierarchy; only leaf accounts postable.
464	
465	All statements build in `finance/service/statements.py` (reporting consumes via `finance/queries.py`) from ONE base aggregate over `fin_journal_lines` only — no header join, because lines denormalize tenant_id, posting_date, fiscal_period_id, is_posted (set during the posting transaction):
466	
467	```python
468	select(JournalLine.account_id,
469	       func.sum(functional_debit_amount - functional_credit_amount))
470	.where(tenant filter, is_posted == True, date predicates)
471	.group_by(account_id)
472	```
473	
474	MoneyType type propagation keeps sums exact on both backends.
475	
476	- **Trial balance** = that query split into per-account debit/credit totals.
477	- **P&L** = REVENUE+EXPENSE over a range.
478	- **Balance sheet** = ASSET/LIABILITY/EQUITY cumulative to a date, with retained earnings computed on the fly as cumulative REVENUE+EXPENSE net over ALL history to the as-of date, presented as a synthetic "Current and accumulated earnings" equity line (exact by construction, since v1 has no year-end carryforward per the parity doc).
479	- **Cash flow (indirect)** = net income + signed deltas of non-cash balance-sheet balances between two as-of dates grouped by cash_flow_category, with the service ASSERTING reconciliation to the movement on is_cash_equivalent accounts equals zero — a built-in self-check.
480	
481	**No stored totals anywhere:** no balance tables, no materialized views (CLAUDE.md rule 1).
482	
483	**Performance:** composite partial index `ix_fin_journal_lines_proj` ON (tenant_id, account_id, posting_date), declared with BOTH `postgresql_where=is_posted` AND `sqlite_where=is_posted` dialect kwargs (each engine needs its own — added; the draft named only one), plus `postgresql_include=['functional_debit_amount','functional_credit_amount']` for index-only scans on PG (kwarg harmlessly ignored on SQLite). Holds sub-second to ~10M lines on Postgres. Escape hatch if scale exceeds that: an explicitly-cache-semantics materialized view refreshed from the journal (journal stays SSOT), out of v1 and gated on a DECISIONS.md entry.
484	
485	The is_posted flag's agreement with header status is guaranteed by the two-flush posting protocol plus immutability triggers and asserted by a dedicated guard test.
486	
487	**Rationale.**
488	Direct implementation of the Universal Journal rule: views are projections, totals never stored, FI/CO reconciliation eliminated by construction. Five account types + cash_flow_category is the minimal metadata from which all four statements derive mechanically; computing retained earnings from full history is what makes "no carryforward in v1" sound rather than a correctness hole. One base query keeps every statement provably consistent with the trial balance — same predicate, same index.
489	
490	**Rejected alternatives.**
491	- Running-balance or period-totals tables updated on posting: violates CLAUDE.md rule 1 verbatim and reintroduces reconciliation.
492	- Account-code-range statement layout (classic SAP FSV intervals): the account_group FK hierarchy is simpler, referentially enforced, template-friendly.
493	- Direct cash-flow method: requires counterparty-cash tagging on every line; indirect derives from data already present.
494	- Materialized views in v1: premature and PG-only.
495	
496	**Risks & mitigations.**
497	- Cumulative-from-genesis balance-sheet queries grow linearly with history until balance carryforward ships (already a parity-doc "later") — the partial covering index keeps this an index-only scan on PG, and the carryforward job slots in later without schema change.
498	
499	---
500	
501	## D-022 — Alembic dual-database strategy and CI matrix
502	
503	**Decision.**
504	A single linear migration chain runs unmodified on both backends; migrations are the ONLY schema source — `Base.metadata.create_all` is banned everywhere INCLUDING tests, because triggers and raw DDL live only in migrations (tests would otherwise pass without the DB guards they claim to test). Rules:
505	
506	1. `env.py` uses the async pattern (`async_engine_from_config` + `connection.run_sync(do_run_migrations)`, `asyncio.run` in the offline-safe wrapper), reads `ATLAS_DATABASE_URL`, configures `compare_type=True` and `render_as_batch=True`.
507	2. Every ALTER goes through `with op.batch_alter_table(...)` unconditionally — pass-through on Postgres, copy-rebuild on SQLite — which requires deterministic constraint names: `core/models.py` declares `MetaData(naming_convention={'ix':'ix_%(column_0_label)s','uq':'uq_%(table_name)s_%(column_0_name)s','ck':'ck_%(table_name)s_%(constraint_name)s','fk':'fk_%(table_name)s_%(column_0_name)s_%(referred_table_name)s','pk':'pk_%(table_name)s'})`; unnamed constraints cannot be dropped in SQLite batch mode.
508	3. Type portability lives in the models (`with_variant` JSONB, `sa.Uuid`, MoneyType/QuantityType/RateType), so autogenerated revisions import those types from `app.core.models` and stay dialect-clean; hand review of every autogen revision is mandatory.
509	4. Trigger/function DDL: per-dialect string pairs side by side in the migration body under `if op.get_bind().dialect.name == 'postgresql': op.execute(PG_SQL) else: op.execute(SQLITE_SQL)`; stable names `trg_<table>_<purpose>`; upgrades DROP TRIGGER IF EXISTS then CREATE; downgrades drop. **Rule (load-bearing):** any migration that batch-alters a trigger-bearing table MUST re-execute that table's trigger DDL afterwards, because SQLite's copy-rebuild silently drops triggers — recorded in the migration template comment and caught by the guard tests, which run against the final migrated schema. Postgres-only physical extras (GIN indexes, INCLUDE columns) sit in the same dialect branch with a plain-index or no-op SQLite arm.
510	5. CI, single `backend` job extended: **step A** `alembic upgrade head` + full `uv run pytest -q` on SQLite (file DB); **step B** `services: postgres:16` container — `alembic upgrade head`, then `alembic downgrade base && alembic upgrade head` (reversibility proof), then `uv run pytest -q -m pg` re-exercising the DB-guard subset (journal/period/audit triggers, JSONB paths, with_for_update contention, idempotency races) on real Postgres. The `pg` marker lives on `tests/modules/finance/test_journal_db_guards.py`, period bypass tests, audit append-only tests, and inventory locking tests.
511	
512	**Rationale.**
513	D-003 fixed the dual-backend posture; this makes it mechanical. Batch-everywhere plus a naming convention is the canonical Alembic SQLite recipe; model-level type variance makes autogenerate output portable by construction; and running the financial-guard tests on real Postgres is what turns "enforced at DB level on BOTH" from an assertion into a tested claim. The trigger-recreation-after-batch rule prevents the silent-guard-loss failure mode that would otherwise pass every test until a rebuild migration ships.
514	
515	**Rejected alternatives.**
516	- Two migration branches per dialect: guaranteed drift, doubled review, breaks linear NNNN numbering.
517	- `create_all` for tests with a trigger fixture: duplicates trigger DDL outside migrations, violating single-source.
518	- Skipping Postgres in CI: trigger and FOR UPDATE behavior differ enough that untested-on-PG is unacceptable for the financial engine.
519	- Separate .sql files for trigger DDL: STRUCTURE forbids orphan files; migrations are self-contained.
520	
521	**Risks & mitigations.**
522	- Per-test isolation against the migrated schema is owned by D-025 (template-copy pattern) — the two decisions interlock and must not drift.
523	- Autogen occasionally emits dialect-specific DDL despite variants — mandatory hand review per STRUCTURE §8.6 plus the dual-engine CI run catches it.
524	
525	---
526	
527	## D-023 — Frontend type strategy (hand-written types.ts with compile-time drift gate)
528	
529	**Decision.**
530	Per STRUCTURE §4, each frontend module keeps a HAND-WRITTEN `src/modules/<module>/types.ts` mirroring that module's backend Pydantic Read/Create/Update/Filter schemas, snake_case preserved (no camelCase translation layer).
531	
532	**Mapping conventions, fixed:** Decimal/money → `string`; date/datetime → `string` (ISO 8601); UUID → `string`; backend enums → TS string-literal unions of the UPPER_SNAKE values (`type EntryStatus = 'DRAFT' | 'POSTED' | 'REVERSED'`); nullable/Optional → `| null`; Masked fields → `T | null`. Shared envelope types (`Page<T> {items, next_cursor, limit}`, `ApiError {error: {code, message, details, request_id}}`) live once in `src/lib/apiClient.ts`.
533	
534	**Drift control, two compile-time gates and zero runtime cost:**
535	
536	1. `backend/openapi.json` is COMMITTED and regenerated via a Makefile target (`make openapi` calls a tiny dump entry that instantiates the app factory and writes `app.openapi()`); a backend pytest test asserts the committed file equals the live app's schema, so any schema change that forgets regeneration fails the backend CI job with a "run make openapi" message.
537	2. A frontend devDependency `openapi-typescript` generates a GITIGNORED `src/lib/openapi.gen.d.ts` from `../backend/openapi.json` as a pre-step of `npm run typecheck`; each module adds a `types.contract.ts` containing only type-level assertions using Expect/Equal helpers from lib (`type _ = Expect<Equal<JournalEntry, components['schemas']['JournalEntryRead']>>`) — one line per mirrored type — so tsc fails on any divergence in either direction.
538	
539	Application code imports ONLY the hand-written `types.ts`; the generated file is referenced solely by contract files and is never committed (consistent with STRUCTURE §8.6: generated files are never hand-edited; here it is also never shipped). The CI frontend job's existing `npm run typecheck` therefore enforces the contract with no new job.
540	
541	**Rationale.**
542	STRUCTURE mandates hand-written mirrors, which keeps frontend types curated and readable — but hand-written without a gate guarantees drift. Routing the gate through the committed OpenAPI document gives an explicit, reviewable contract artifact whose own freshness is enforced backend-side, while the type-level Equal assertions catch field renames, nullability changes, and enum-value drift at compile time in both directions. String-typed money/dates align with the backend's Decimal-as-string serialization and force all formatting through `lib/format.ts` per STRUCTURE.
543	
544	**Rejected alternatives.**
545	- Fully generated committed types as the app's source: violates the hand-written mandate, bloats diffs, and produces unidiomatic deeply-nested component types.
546	- Runtime zod/valibot validation: a second schema source to keep in sync and runtime cost on every response; the API is first-party so compile-time checking suffices.
547	- No gate ("be careful"): drift is guaranteed across 13 modules.
548	- Comparing types via a custom AST script: reimplements what tsc's structural equality already does.
549	
550	**Risks & mitigations.**
551	- `openapi.json` merge conflicts on parallel schema work — resolved by regenerating (`make openapi`), never hand-merging.
552	- Contract files add one assertion line per type — trivial, and a missing assertion is visible in review because the convention is one contract file per module listed beside `types.ts`.
553	- `Equal<>` on very large unions can slow tsc marginally — bounded by module-scoped contract files.
554	
555	---
556	
557	## D-024 — Frontend auth: in-memory access token, cookie refresh, cross-tab single-flight
558	
559	**Decision.**
560	`src/lib/auth.ts` owns all token state. **Access token:** held ONLY in a module-scoped variable (with a subscribe hook for React state) — never localStorage/sessionStorage. **Refresh token:** never touched by JS (httpOnly cookie managed by the browser, scoped to `/api/v1/auth` per D-008). `apiClient.ts` attaches `Authorization: Bearer` from auth.ts on every call.
561	
562	- **Boot sequence:** app start calls `POST /api/v1/auth/refresh` once (cookie present → new access+refresh pair, resumes the session silently; 401 → unauthenticated state, router redirects to /login).
563	- **Proactive renewal:** auth.ts decodes the access token's exp claim client-side (base64 decode only, no verification — it is not a trust decision) and schedules a refresh at exp minus 60 s.
564	- **Reactive path:** on any 401, apiClient triggers a single-flight refresh — within a tab, concurrent requests await one shared in-flight promise then retry exactly once; a second 401 after retry → hard logout.
565	- **Cross-tab coordination** (required because backend rotation invalidates the old refresh jti — even with the 10 s grace window, uncoordinated tabs hammering refresh is wrong): the refresher acquires `navigator.locks.request('atlas-auth-refresh')` so exactly one tab rotates, and broadcasts the new access token via `BroadcastChannel('atlas-auth')`; other tabs adopt it instead of refreshing; logout events broadcast the same way so all tabs clear state and redirect together.
566	- **Logout:** `POST /api/v1/auth/logout` (revokes the sid row, clears the cookie), clear memory, broadcast, `queryClient.clear()`.
567	- **Identity/permissions:** after any successful login/refresh-boot, fetch `GET /api/v1/auth/me` (user, tenant, permission keys) into TanStack Query; TanStack Router `beforeLoad` guards check auth.ts state and the permission set for route gating — UI-only convenience, the server remains the enforcement point.
568	- **Tenant selection** happens at login (tenant_slug field); the SPA never sends tenant headers — tenancy rides the JWT.
569	
570	**Rationale.**
571	Memory-only access tokens are XSS-resistant (no persistent readable storage) and the boot-refresh makes hard reloads seamless since the httpOnly cookie persists. Single-flight + Web Locks + BroadcastChannel is the standard answer to rotation-with-reuse-detection in multi-tab SPAs: it eliminates the benign-race family revocations the backend grace window only softens. Proactive renewal avoids latency spikes and thundering 401 retries. Keeping every fetch in apiClient.ts (per STRUCTURE) means the 401/retry/refresh logic exists exactly once.
572	
573	**Rejected alternatives.**
574	- localStorage/sessionStorage tokens: XSS-exfiltratable, explicitly rejected.
575	- Access token in a cookie too: makes every API call CSRF-relevant instead of just /auth.
576	- Per-tab independent refresh without coordination: races rotation and logs users out under normal multi-tab use.
577	- Service-worker token broker: strictly more moving parts for the same isolation in a v1 SPA.
578	- Storing permissions in localStorage for instant boot: stale-permission UI and another sync problem — /auth/me is one cheap request.
579	
580	**Risks & mitigations.**
581	- `navigator.locks`/BroadcastChannel need modern browsers — fine for v1 scope; a no-op fallback (per-tab single-flight only) keeps Safari/old engines working with the backend grace window absorbing the residual race.
582	- In-memory token dies on reload — by design; boot refresh restores it.
583	- Clock skew breaks proactive scheduling — harmless: the reactive 401 path is the safety net.
584	
585	---
586	
587	## D-025 — Backend testing strategy (async fixtures, per-test DB copies, trigger tests on SQLite)
588	
589	**Decision.**
590	pytest + pytest-asyncio with `asyncio_mode=auto`; HTTP tests use `httpx.AsyncClient` over `ASGITransport(app)` — no live server.
591	
592	**Database isolation uses the TEMPLATE-COPY pattern**, deliberately replacing the draft's SAVEPOINT/join-external-transaction approach, which breaks the moment code under test performs REAL commits — and ours does by design (idempotency's separate reservation transaction, `run_in_uow` commits, numbering claims): a session-scoped fixture builds ONE migrated template SQLite file via programmatic `alembic.command.upgrade(config, 'head')` (env.py's `asyncio.run` pattern works because the session fixture runs outside any event loop); a function-scoped fixture copies that file (`shutil.copy`, ~ms) into tmp_path, builds an aiosqlite engine on the copy with the connect-event `PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON`, and overrides the app's session dependency. Every test gets a fully migrated, trigger-bearing, fresh database where real commits are allowed and nothing leaks across tests. For the pg-marked subset in CI, a fixture creates a per-test database via `CREATE DATABASE ... TEMPLATE atlas_test_template` from a once-migrated template database and drops it after — same semantics on Postgres.
593	
594	**Fixtures in `tests/conftest.py`:** `tenant_factory` provisions tenant + admin user + role with named permissions through the REAL provisioning service under `system_context`, returning a handle with tenant_id and an `auth_headers(user)` helper that performs a real login; `authed_client` composes it; `permissions_context` sets the `current_permissions` ContextVar for serializer-level masking tests; module fixtures live in `tests/modules/<module>/conftest.py` per STRUCTURE §6.
595	
596	**DB-guard tests** (`tests/modules/finance/test_journal_db_guards.py` etc.) deliberately use raw `session.execute(text(...))` to BYPASS the service layer — sanctioned because the CI grep gate banning `text()` is scoped to `app/`, not `tests/` — asserting that UPDATE/DELETE on posted lines, unbalanced DRAFT→POSTED, closed-period posting, and audit UPDATE/DELETE all raise with the `ATLAS_` tokens on SQLite, with the same tests re-run on Postgres via `-m pg`. The tenancy suite enumerates `Base.registry.mappers` (auto-covering new models); event-bus tests assert handler effects and rollback-on-handler-failure within one transaction; idempotency tests exercise the two-transaction reservation flow with real commits; determinism comes from explicit posting_date/anchor arguments in factories, not clock freezing.
597	
598	**Rationale.**
599	The template-copy pattern is the single decision that makes everything else testable as designed: SAVEPOINT isolation silently converts the idempotency guard's real COMMIT into a savepoint release (changing the very semantics under test) and shares state when code opens a second session. File copies are milliseconds on SQLite and CREATE DATABASE TEMPLATE is fast on Postgres, so the cost is negligible while every test sees the exact schema migrations produce — triggers included, which is the whole point of asserting DB guards in CI. Factories going through real services means tenancy stamping, numbering, docflow, and audit are exercised by every test that touches data.
600	
601	**Rejected alternatives.**
602	- SAVEPOINT/join-external-transaction per test (the draft): incompatible with real multi-transaction code paths and second sessions; rejected as the primary pattern.
603	- `create_all` + trigger fixture: duplicates DDL outside migrations and tests a schema nobody ships.
604	- In-memory `:memory:` SQLite: cannot be shared across connections/sessions the way the app's engine needs, and cannot be template-copied.
605	- One shared DB with truncation between tests: ordering-sensitive and slow on Postgres.
606	
607	**Risks & mitigations.**
608	- Session-scoped template means schema changes require fixture cache invalidation — the template path embeds the Alembic head revision in its filename, so a new revision automatically rebuilds.
609	- Per-test PG database creation is slower (~100 ms each) — confined to the small pg-marked subset.
610	- Raw-SQL bypass tests are tightly coupled to trigger names/tokens — intentional pinning; they exist to fail when guards change.
611	
612	---
613	
614	## D-026 — Seed-data architecture (deterministic, per-template, three months of linked transactions)
615	
616	**Decision.**
617	`backend/seed.py` is a CLI (argparse: `--templates` defaulting to all five industry templates, `--anchor-date` defaulting to today, `--reset`) that assumes a migrated database (Makefile target chains `alembic upgrade head`).
618	
619	**Determinism:** one `random.Random(f'{template}:{anchor_date}')` per tenant — identical output for a given (template, anchor) pair; the anchor is recorded on the tenant so reruns are reproducible for bug reports.
620	
621	**Provisioning phase** under `system_context()`: per template, create tenant (slug `demo-<template>`, fixed admin credentials sourced from `.env.example` values), apply the YAML industry template via the industry module's real application service — modules toggled, display labels, chart-of-accounts preset, tax codes, number-sequence patterns, system roles, custom-field defs (written through `core/custom_fields.py`).
622	
623	**Transaction phase:** set the tenancy ContextVar to the tenant (NOT `system_context` — business writes must be stamped and filtered normally) and drive everything through the REAL service layer wrapped in `run_in_uow()`, never raw inserts — so numbering, docflow registration and links, domain events (goods issue → COGS), audit rows, and DB triggers all fire exactly as in production, making seed a standing integration proof.
624	
625	**Script per template spans 3 calendar months ending at anchor:** master data first (items, vendors, customers, warehouses, employees, WBS elements, exchange rates including one foreign currency); then interlinked flows — procurement P2P chains (requisition → PO → goods receipt → AP invoice → payment run), sales O2C (quote → order → delivery → customer invoice → receipt, including partial shipments and one open backorder), template-specific depth (production orders with WIP postings for manufacturing; projects + timesheets for professional-services; maintenance orders for construction; quality inspection lots for healthcare/retail receiving), foreign-currency invoices plus a month-end FX revaluation run, manual journal entries, and month-end closes: periods for months 1 and 2 CLOSED via the real period-close service, month 3 left OPEN with open AP/AR items so aging, dunning, and dashboards have live data. Volumes ~100-300 documents per tenant (seconds on SQLite).
626	
627	**Idempotency:** without `--reset`, seed refuses if a demo tenant exists; `--reset` hard-deletes the demo tenants by cascade — the ONLY sanctioned hard-delete path in the codebase, running under `system_context` and documented as such.
628	
629	**Self-verification:** seed ends by asserting, per tenant, (a) trial balance debits == credits, (b) every created document's docflow chain traverses end-to-end, (c) inventory GL balance == sum of `inv_item_valuations` — and CI runs seed against SQLite after the test suite as a smoke gate.
630	
631	**Rationale.**
632	Seeding through real services is the load-bearing choice: SQL-dump seeds rot with every migration and bypass exactly the invariants (gapless numbers, docflow, COGS events, period triggers) the demo exists to showcase, while service-driven seeding doubles as an end-to-end integration test the CI runs for free. Deterministic RNG + recorded anchor gives reproducible demos and bug reports without freezing real time. Closing two of three months demonstrates the period-close machinery and leaves believable open items for the operational screens.
633	
634	**Rejected alternatives.**
635	- SQL dump / fixtures files: bypass invariants, drift with schema, undebuggable diffs.
636	- Faker with random seed-per-run: non-reproducible demo states.
637	- Seeding via HTTP API: needs a running server and auth choreography for zero added fidelity — the service layer is the contract.
638	- A full year of data: slower seeds for no demo value; the parity scope's reports all read well at 3 months.
639	
640	**Risks & mitigations.**
641	- Anchor defaulting to today means runs on different days differ in dates (structure stays identical given anchor) — acceptable; CI pins a fixed anchor for the smoke gate.
642	- Seed duration creeps as modules land — bounded by per-tenant volume caps and the CI timing check.
643	- The `--reset` cascade is a footgun if pointed at a non-demo tenant — guarded by a slug prefix check (refuses anything not starting with `demo-`).
644

1	"""Chart of accounts (D-021) and fiscal years/periods (D-018).
2	
3	One of two files in the finance ``models/`` package (STRUCTURE §3 split: the universal-journal
4	models in ``models/journal.py`` pushed the combined file over the 400-line cap). The package
5	``__init__`` re-exports both so ``from app.modules.finance.models import Account`` is unchanged.
6	
7	Per D-021 the account-type model here is exactly what later statement projections consume:
8	``account_type`` drives every statement (trial balance, P&L, balance sheet, cash flow), the
9	``account_group`` tree is a PURE PRESENTATION hierarchy (accounts hang off groups; the
10	hierarchy lives on the GROUP tree's ``parent_id``, not on accounts — so accounts have no
11	``parent_id``, resolving the task's "parent_id OR account_group" choice in favour of D-021),
12	and ``cash_flow_category`` + ``is_cash_equivalent`` feed the indirect cash-flow statement.
13	
14	Enum-valued columns are plain ``sa.String`` storing the StrEnum's UPPER_SNAKE value, matching
15	how core stores status values (no ``sa.Enum``); the service maps to/from the constants classes.
16	All four tables follow the D-007 composite-tenant-FK backstop: tenant_unique() on every table
17	that is referenced, tenant_fk() composites for every cross-row link so a child can never point
18	at another tenant's parent.
19	"""

28	    AuditMixin,
29	    Base,
30	    TenantMixin,
31	    TimestampMixin,
32	    UuidPKMixin,
33	    tenant_fk,
34	    tenant_unique,

39	class AccountGroup(UuidPKMixin, TenantMixin, AuditMixin, TimestampMixin, Base):
40	    """A node in the chart-of-accounts presentation hierarchy (D-021). Pure presentation:
41	    groups carry no postings and no balances; ``parent_id`` builds the tree and accounts
42	    reference a group via ``account_group_id``. ``sort_order`` orders siblings in the UI.
43	    Audited (D-010): the COA layout is configuration."""

45	    __tablename__ = "fin_account_groups"
46	    __table_args__ = (
47	        sa.UniqueConstraint("tenant_id", "code", name="uq_fin_account_groups_tenant_id_code"),
48	        tenant_unique(),

50	        # Self-referential composite tenant FK: a group's parent must be in the same tenant.
51	        tenant_fk("fin_account_groups", "parent_id"),

54	    code: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(sa.String(40), nullable=False)

1	"""Finance's cross-module read interface (STRUCTURE §5).
2	
3	Finance is the bottom of the dependency order: every other module (inventory, sales, ...)
4	may import THIS file to read finance state synchronously, and finance imports no other
5	module's queries. Keep this surface thin and stable — it is a contract. The journal posting
6	flow (4.2) calls ``find_period_for_date`` to resolve an entry's period from its posting_date;
7	inventory/sales call ``get_period_status`` to refuse stock/sales documents dated into a closed
8	period before they reach the GL.
9	
10	Every function takes an explicit ``tenant_id`` and runs under the caller's tenant context, so
11	the D-007 filter applies on top of the explicit predicate — these are ordinary tenant-scoped
12	ORM reads, not a bypass.
13	"""
14	
15	import uuid
16	from datetime import date
17	from decimal import Decimal
18	
19	from sqlalchemy import func, select
20	from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession
21	
22	from app.modules.finance.constants import (
23	    BillStatus,
24	    InvoiceStatus,
25	    PeriodStatus,
26	    RateKind,
27	    TaxDirection,
28	)
29	from app.modules.finance.models import (
30	    Account,
31	    CostCenter,
32	    CustomerInvoice,
33	    FiscalPeriod,
34	    JournalLine,
35	    ProfitCenter,
36	    TaxCode,
37	    VendorBill,
38	)
39	from app.modules.finance.service import fx as _fx
40	from app.modules.finance.service import tax as _tax
41	from app.modules.finance.service.tax import TaxCalculation
42	
43	
44	async def find_period_for_date(
45	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, on_date: date
46	) -> FiscalPeriod | None:
47	    """The fiscal period whose [start_date, end_date] (inclusive) covers ``on_date``, or
48	    None if no period does. Periods within a year are contiguous and non-overlapping (the
49	    service enforces that on generation), so at most one matches. This is the date->period
50	    lookup the journal uses on every posting (4.2)."""
51	    stmt = select(FiscalPeriod).where(
52	        FiscalPeriod.tenant_id == tenant_id,
53	        FiscalPeriod.start_date <= on_date,
54	        FiscalPeriod.end_date >= on_date,
55	    )
56	    return (await session.execute(stmt)).scalar_one_or_none()
57	
58	
59	async def get_period_status(
60	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, on_date: date
61	) -> PeriodStatus | None:
62	    """The OPEN/CLOSED status of the period covering ``on_date``, or None when no period
63	    covers it. Callers posting financial or stock documents check this up front: None or
64	    CLOSED means the date is not in an open period and the document must be rejected
65	    (the DB-level period trigger on the journal in 4.2 is the bypass-proof backstop)."""
66	    period = await find_period_for_date(session, tenant_id, on_date)
67	    if period is None:
68	        return None
69	    return PeriodStatus(period.status)
70	
71	
72	async def account_exists(
73	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, code: str
74	) -> bool:
75	    """Whether an account with ``code`` exists in the tenant's chart of accounts. Lets
76	    another module validate a referenced account code without importing finance models."""
77	    stmt = select(Account.id).where(
78	        Account.tenant_id == tenant_id, Account.code == code
79	    )
80	    return (await session.execute(stmt)).first() is not None
81	
82	
83	async def get_rate(
84	    session: AsyncSession,
85	    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
86	    from_code: str,
87	    to_code: str,
88	    on_date: date,
89	    rate_type: RateKind = RateKind.SPOT,
90	) -> Decimal:
91	    """The exchange rate to convert ``from_code`` into ``to_code`` on ``on_date`` (D-019). Exposed
92	    here so other modules price in functional terms (AP/AR/inventory translate at this rate); a
93	    missing rate raises (postings never guess). Same contract as service/fx.get_rate."""
94	    return await _fx.get_rate(session, tenant_id, from_code, to_code, on_date, rate_type)
95	
96	
97	async def functional_currency(session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID) -> str:
98	    """The tenant's functional (reporting) currency code (D-019). Exposed so other modules know the
99	    currency every functional amount is denominated in. Raises if none is configured."""
100	    return await _fx.functional_currency(session, tenant_id)
101	
102	
103	async def get_tax_code(
104	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, code: str
105	) -> TaxCode | None:
106	    """The tax code with ``code`` in the tenant's catalog, or None (PLAN 4.4). Sales/Procurement
107	    resolve a line's tax code by its short key (e.g. ``'VAT20'``) through this contract rather than
108	    importing finance models — finance is the bottom of the dependency order (STRUCTURE §5)."""
109	    stmt = select(TaxCode).where(TaxCode.tenant_id == tenant_id, TaxCode.code == code)
110	    return (await session.execute(stmt)).scalar_one_or_none()
111	
112	
113	def calculate_line_tax(
114	    base_amount: Decimal,
115	    tax_code: TaxCode,
116	    *,
117	    direction: TaxDirection,
118	    currency_code: str = "USD",
119	) -> TaxCalculation:
120	    """Tax one line consistently for any module (PLAN 4.4). A thin, pure re-export of
121	    ``service.tax.calculate_line_tax`` so Sales/Procurement compute net/tax/gross + the tax account
122	    exactly as finance does — one tax engine, no duplicated math. ``base_amount`` is the gross when
123	    the code is inclusive else the net; all amounts quantize to ``currency_code``'s minor unit."""
124	    return _tax.calculate_line_tax(
125	        base_amount, tax_code, direction=direction, currency_code=currency_code
126	    )
127	
128	
129	async def get_open_vendor_bills(
130	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, partner_id: uuid.UUID
131	) -> list[VendorBill]:
132	    """A partner's POSTED vendor bills that still have an open balance (PLAN 4.5, D-029). Exposed
133	    so procurement (later) can read a vendor's open AP without importing finance models — finance
134	    is the bottom of the dependency order (STRUCTURE §5). Keyed by the opaque ``partner_id``; never
135	    an FK to a vendor master. Ordered by due date so the oldest-due bills surface first."""
136	    stmt = (
137	        select(VendorBill)
138	        .where(
139	            VendorBill.tenant_id == tenant_id,
140	            VendorBill.partner_id == partner_id,
141	            VendorBill.status.in_(
142	                (BillStatus.POSTED.value, BillStatus.PARTIALLY_PAID.value)
143	            ),
144	            VendorBill.open_amount > 0,
145	        )
146	        .order_by(VendorBill.due_date)
147	    )
148	    return list((await session.execute(stmt)).scalars().all())
149	
150	
151	def _open_customer_invoices_stmt(tenant_id: uuid.UUID, partner_id: uuid.UUID):
152	    """The SELECT for a partner's open customer invoices (PLAN 4.6, D-029): POSTED/PARTIALLY_PAID
153	    with a positive open balance, oldest-due first. Shared by the list + the balance sum so they
154	    can never disagree."""
155	    return (
156	        select(CustomerInvoice)
157	        .where(
158	            CustomerInvoice.tenant_id == tenant_id,
159	            CustomerInvoice.partner_id == partner_id,
160	            CustomerInvoice.status.in_(
161	                (InvoiceStatus.POSTED.value, InvoiceStatus.PARTIALLY_PAID.value)
162	            ),
163	            CustomerInvoice.open_amount > 0,
164	        )
165	        .order_by(CustomerInvoice.due_date)
166	    )
167	
168	
169	async def get_open_customer_invoices(
170	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, partner_id: uuid.UUID
171	) -> list[CustomerInvoice]:
172	    """A partner's POSTED customer invoices that still have an open balance (PLAN 4.6, D-029).
173	    Exposed so sales (later) can read a customer's open AR without importing finance models —
174	    finance is the bottom of the dependency order (STRUCTURE §5). Keyed by the opaque
175	    ``partner_id``; never an FK to a customer master. Ordered oldest-due first."""
176	    stmt = _open_customer_invoices_stmt(tenant_id, partner_id)
177	    return list((await session.execute(stmt)).scalars().all())
178	
179	
180	async def customer_open_balance(
181	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, partner_id: uuid.UUID
182	) -> Decimal:
183	    """The total still-owed AR for a partner across all open invoices (PLAN 4.6, D-029): the sum of
184	    their ``open_amount`` in transaction currency. Exposed so Sales' credit-limit block can ask
185	    finance "how much does this customer currently owe?" without importing finance models — the
186	    bottom-dependency contract (STRUCTURE §5). Sums in Python over the (typically small) open set so
187	    the exact-decimal MoneyType round-trips identically on both engines (D-015). Returns 0 for a
188	    partner with no open invoices."""
189	    invoices = await get_open_customer_invoices(session, tenant_id, partner_id)
190	    return sum((Decimal(str(inv.open_amount)) for inv in invoices), Decimal(0))
191	
192	
193	# --- Controlling: dimension validation + cost-centre balance (PLAN 4.7) -------
194	
195	
196	async def cost_center_exists(
197	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, cost_center_id: uuid.UUID
198	) -> bool:
199	    """Whether a cost centre with ``cost_center_id`` exists in the tenant. The journal posting flow
200	    calls this to validate a line's ``cost_center_id`` dimension before the line is written —
201	    service-level dimension integrity replacing the absent FK on the trigger-bearing journal-lines
202	    table (D-022)."""
203	    stmt = select(CostCenter.id).where(
204	        CostCenter.tenant_id == tenant_id, CostCenter.id == cost_center_id
205	    )
206	    return (await session.execute(stmt)).first() is not None
207	
208	
209	async def profit_center_exists(
210	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, profit_center_id: uuid.UUID
211	) -> bool:
212	    """Whether a profit centre with ``profit_center_id`` exists in the tenant. The companion to
213	    ``cost_center_exists`` for the journal line's ``profit_center_id`` dimension (D-022)."""
214	    stmt = select(ProfitCenter.id).where(
215	        ProfitCenter.tenant_id == tenant_id, ProfitCenter.id == profit_center_id
216	    )
217	    return (await session.execute(stmt)).first() is not None
218	
219	
220	async def cost_center_balance(
221	    session: AsyncSession,
222	    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
223	    cost_center_id: uuid.UUID,
224	    period_id: uuid.UUID,
225	) -> Decimal:
226	    """The cost centre's NET functional balance for a fiscal period (PLAN 4.7): SUM over POSTED
227	    journal lines carrying this ``cost_center_id`` in ``period_id`` of (functional debit minus
228	    functional credit). This is the amount ``run_allocation`` redistributes — CO is a projection of
229	    the journal (D-021), so the balance is derived from journal lines, never a stored total.
230	    MoneyType type propagation keeps the SUM exact on both engines (D-015); returns 0 when none."""
231	    debit = func.coalesce(
232	        func.sum(JournalLine.functional_debit_amount), 0
233	    )
234	    credit = func.coalesce(
235	        func.sum(JournalLine.functional_credit_amount), 0
236	    )
237	    stmt = select(debit - credit).where(
238	        JournalLine.tenant_id == tenant_id,
239	        JournalLine.cost_center_id == cost_center_id,
240	        JournalLine.fiscal_period_id == period_id,
241	        JournalLine.is_posted.is_(True),
242	    )
243	    result = (await session.execute(stmt)).scalar_one()
244	    return Decimal(str(result)) if result is not None else Decimal(0)
245	
246	
247	# --- Statements: the base aggregate, exposed for reporting reuse (PLAN 4.8, D-021) -----------
248	
249	
250	async def account_balances(
251	    session: AsyncSession,
252	    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
253	    *,
254	    date_to: date,
255	    date_from: date | None = None,
256	) -> dict[uuid.UUID, Decimal]:
257	    """Signed (debit-positive) net balance per account over the posted journal (D-021). The single
258	    statement base aggregate, exposed here so the reporting module (PLAN 13) builds its own views as
259	    projections of the SAME query the statements use — never a stored total. ``date_from`` bounds
260	    the range (a P&L-style window); omit it for cumulative-to-date balances (balance-sheet-style).
261	    Thin re-export of ``service.statements._account_balances`` — one aggregate, one index."""
262	    from app.modules.finance.service.statements import _account_balances
263	
264	    return await _account_balances(
265	        session, tenant_id, date_to=date_to, date_from=date_from
266	    )
267	
268	
269	async def net_income(
270	    session: AsyncSession,
271	    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
272	    *,
273	    date_to: date,
274	    date_from: date | None = None,
275	) -> Decimal:
276	    """Net income (revenue - expense, credit-positive so a profit is positive) over the range
277	    (D-021). Derived from ``account_balances`` + account types so reporting reads it as a projection
278	    of the journal — the same figure the balance sheet folds into retained earnings. Cumulative to
279	    ``date_to`` when ``date_from`` is omitted."""
280	    from app.modules.finance.service.statements import net_income_signed
281	    from app.modules.finance.service.statements.base import load_account_meta
282	
283	    balances = await account_balances(
284	        session, tenant_id, date_to=date_to, date_from=date_from
285	    )
286	    meta = await load_account_meta(session, tenant_id)
287	    return net_income_signed(balances, meta)

1	"""Chart-of-accounts business logic (D-021): accounts and the presentation-group tree.
2	
3	The service layer owns every rule (CLAUDE.md rule 7); the router stays thin.
4	
5	- accounts: normal_balance defaults from account_type (D-021) so the stored side can never
6	  disagree with the type; code uniqueness is the DB UNIQUE(tenant_id, code) constraint,
7	  surfaced here as a ConflictError before the flush would raise.
8	- account groups: a presentation tree (D-021) with cycle protection — a group can never be
9	  its own ancestor.
10	
11	``from __future__ import annotations`` keeps annotations as strings so ``Page[Account]`` (the
12	ORM model) is never evaluated into a Pydantic schema at import — ``Account`` is a SQLAlchemy
13	model, not a Pydantic one; the router re-validates the page items into ``AccountRead``.
14	"""
15	
16	from __future__ import annotations
17	
18	import uuid
19	
20	from sqlalchemy import select
21	from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession
22	
23	from app.core.exceptions import ConflictError, NotFoundError, ValidationFailedError
24	from app.core.pagination import (
25	    DEFAULT_LIMIT,

27	    SortDirection,

37	)
38	from app.modules.finance.models import Account, AccountGroup
39	from app.modules.finance.schemas import (

49	) -> Account | None:

56	) -> Account:

59	        raise NotFoundError(message="Account not found", code="finance.account_not_found")

64	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, payload: AccountCreate
65	) -> Account:
66	    """Create a GL account (D-021). Defaults normal_balance from account_type when the
67	    caller omits it; rejects a duplicate code with a ConflictError (the DB UNIQUE is the
68	    backstop). Validates that a referenced account group exists in the tenant."""
69	    if await _account_by_code(session, tenant_id, payload.code) is not None:
70	        raise ConflictError(
71	            message=f"An account with code {payload.code} already exists",
72	            code="finance.account_code_conflict",
73	            details={"code": payload.code},
74	        )
75	    if payload.account_group_id is not None:
76	        await _require_group(session, tenant_id, payload.account_group_id)
77	
78	    account_type = AccountType(payload.account_type)
79	    normal_balance = (
80	        NormalBalance(payload.normal_balance)
81	        if payload.normal_balance is not None
82	        else normal_balance_for(account_type)
83	    )
84	    cash_flow = (
85	        CashFlowCategory(payload.cash_flow_category).value
86	        if payload.cash_flow_category is not None
87	        else None
88	    )
89	    account = Account(
90	        tenant_id=tenant_id,

93	        account_type=account_type.value,
94	        normal_balance=normal_balance.value,
95	        is_postable=payload.is_postable,
96	        cash_flow_category=cash_flow,
97	        is_cash_equivalent=payload.is_cash_equivalent,
98	        account_group_id=payload.account_group_id,
99	        is_active=payload.is_active,
100	        is_monetary=payload.is_monetary,
101	        currency_code=payload.currency_code,
102	    )

111	    account_id: uuid.UUID,

113	) -> Account:
114	    """Partial update of an account's mutable fields (D-010: mutate the loaded object so the
115	    audit diff is captured). code and account_type are immutable and absent from the schema."""
116	    account = await get_account(session, tenant_id, account_id)

170	async def _require_group(
171	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, group_id: uuid.UUID
172	) -> AccountGroup:
173	    group = await session.get(AccountGroup, group_id)
174	    if group is None or group.tenant_id != tenant_id:

181	async def create_account_group(
182	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, payload: AccountGroupCreate
183	) -> AccountGroup:
184	    """Create a presentation-hierarchy group (D-021). Validates the parent exists in the
185	    tenant; a top-level group passes parent_id=None. (A new group has no children yet, so
186	    no cycle is possible at creation — the cycle guard lives in reparenting below.)"""
187	    existing = (
188	        await session.execute(
189	            select(AccountGroup).where(
190	                AccountGroup.tenant_id == tenant_id, AccountGroup.code == payload.code
191	            )
192	        )
193	    ).scalar_one_or_none()
194	    if existing is not None:
195	        raise ConflictError(
196	            message=f"An account group with code {payload.code} already exists",
197	            code="finance.account_group_code_conflict",
198	            details={"code": payload.code},
199	        )
200	    if payload.parent_id is not None:
201	        await _require_group(session, tenant_id, payload.parent_id)
202	    group = AccountGroup(
203	        tenant_id=tenant_id,
204	        code=payload.code,
205	        name=payload.name,
206	        parent_id=payload.parent_id,
207	        sort_order=payload.sort_order,
208	    )
209	    session.add(group)
210	    await session.flush()
211	    return group

214	async def reparent_account_group(
215	    session: AsyncSession,
216	    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
217	    group_id: uuid.UUID,
218	    new_parent_id: uuid.UUID | None,
219	) -> AccountGroup:
220	    """Move a group under a new parent, rejecting any move that would create a cycle — a
221	    group can never be its own ancestor (D-021: the tree must stay a tree)."""
222	    group = await _require_group(session, tenant_id, group_id)
223	    if new_parent_id is not None:
224	        if new_parent_id == group_id:
225	            raise ValidationFailedError(
226	                message="A group cannot be its own parent",
227	                code="finance.account_group_cycle",
228	            )
229	        await _require_group(session, tenant_id, new_parent_id)
230	        await _assert_no_cycle(session, tenant_id, group_id, new_parent_id)
231	    group.parent_id = new_parent_id
232	    await session.flush()
233	    return group
234	
235	
236	async def _assert_no_cycle(
237	    session: AsyncSession,
238	    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
239	    group_id: uuid.UUID,
240	    new_parent_id: uuid.UUID,
241	) -> None:
242	    """Raise if making ``group_id`` a child of ``new_parent_id`` would form a cycle: walk
243	    from new_parent up its parent chain; reaching group_id means group_id is already an
244	    ancestor of the prospective parent. A visited set bounds a pre-existing malformed tree."""
245	    current: uuid.UUID | None = new_parent_id
246	    visited: set[uuid.UUID] = set()
247	    while current is not None:
248	        if current == group_id:
249	            raise ValidationFailedError(
250	                message="Reparenting would create a cycle in the account-group tree",
251	                code="finance.account_group_cycle",
252	            )
253	        if current in visited:
254	            break
255	        visited.add(current)
256	        parent = await _require_group(session, tenant_id, current)
257	        current = parent.parent_id
258	
259	
260	async def list_account_groups(
261	    session: AsyncSession,
262	    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
263	    *,
264	    cursor: str | None = None,
265	    limit: int = DEFAULT_LIMIT,
266	) -> Page[AccountGroup]:
267	    """Keyset-paginated groups, ordered for stable tree rendering (sort_order, code, id
268	    tiebreaker). Paginated like every other collection endpoint (PERFORMANCE §3 / #27)."""
269	    stmt = select(AccountGroup).where(AccountGroup.tenant_id == tenant_id)
270	    return await paginate(
271	        session,
272	        stmt,
273	        order_by=[
274	            OrderKey(AccountGroup.sort_order, SortDirection.ASC),
275	            OrderKey(AccountGroup.code, SortDirection.ASC),
276	        ],
277	        pk=AccountGroup.id,
278	        cursor=cursor,
279	        limit=limit,
280	    )

1	"""Declarative Base with the D-022 naming convention and shared model mixins."""
2	
3	import uuid
4	from datetime import UTC, datetime
5	from typing import Any
6	
7	import sqlalchemy as sa
8	from sqlalchemy.dialects import postgresql
9	from sqlalchemy.orm import DeclarativeBase, Mapped, declared_attr, mapped_column
10	
11	# Deterministic constraint names are mandatory: SQLite batch-mode migrations
12	# cannot drop unnamed constraints (D-022).
13	NAMING_CONVENTION = {
14	    "ix": "ix_%(column_0_label)s",
15	    "uq": "uq_%(table_name)s_%(column_0_name)s",
16	    "ck": "ck_%(table_name)s_%(constraint_name)s",
17	    "fk": "fk_%(table_name)s_%(column_0_name)s_%(referred_table_name)s",
18	    "pk": "pk_%(table_name)s",
19	}
20	
21	# Portable JSON: JSONB on Postgres, plain JSON elsewhere. Type variance lives in
22	# the models so migrations import it from here and stay dialect-clean (D-022).
23	JSON_VARIANT = sa.JSON().with_variant(postgresql.JSONB(), "postgresql")
24	
25	
26	class Base(DeclarativeBase):
27	    metadata = sa.MetaData(naming_convention=NAMING_CONVENTION)
28	
29	
30	class UuidPKMixin:
31	    """uuid4 primary key, client-generated so ids are portable across both engines."""
32	
33	    id: Mapped[uuid.UUID] = mapped_column(sa.Uuid, primary_key=True, default=uuid.uuid4)
34	
35	
36	class TenantMixin:
37	    """Row-level tenancy marker (D-007). Filtering and stamping are enforced by the
38	    core/tenancy.py session listeners; query authors never touch tenant_id."""
39	
40	    @declared_attr
41	    def tenant_id(cls) -> Mapped[uuid.UUID]:
42	        return mapped_column(sa.Uuid, nullable=False, index=True)
43	
44	
45	class AuditMixin:
46	    """Marker mixin (D-010): tags a model for split-phase audit capture. It adds NO
47	    columns — the audit listeners in core/audit.py test ``isinstance(obj, AuditMixin)``
48	    to decide which INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE flushes land in core_audit_log. Per-column
49	    opt-outs are declared on the model via ``__audit_exclude__`` (a frozenset of
50	    attribute names); ``password_hash`` is excluded there on User."""
51	
52	    # Attribute names never written to the diff (D-010: password_hash always). Models
53	    # override by setting their own frozenset; the listeners read it via getattr.
54	    __audit_exclude__: frozenset[str] = frozenset()
55	
56	
57	def utcnow() -> datetime:
58	    """Canonical timestamp source for every SQLAlchemy write (#34)."""
59	    return datetime.now(UTC)
60	
61	
62	class TimestampMixin:
63	    """Timezone-aware UTC stamps, ALWAYS Python-written (#34).
64	
65	    The Python ``default``/``onupdate`` fire for ORM and Core inserts alike, so every
66	    stored value uses SQLAlchemy's canonical SQLite string format (six-digit
67	    microseconds). The DDL ``server_default`` remains only as a fallback for raw SQL
68	    outside SQLAlchemy and must never be relied on: SQLite's CURRENT_TIMESTAMP writes
69	    second-precision strings whose lexicographic comparison against bound datetimes
70	    breaks keyset-pagination equality — the #34 infinite-page-loop bug."""
71	
72	    created_at: Mapped[datetime] = mapped_column(
73	        sa.DateTime(timezone=True),
74	        nullable=False,
75	        default=utcnow,
76	        server_default=sa.func.now(),
77	    )
78	    updated_at: Mapped[datetime] = mapped_column(
79	        sa.DateTime(timezone=True),
80	        nullable=False,
81	        default=utcnow,
82	        server_default=sa.func.now(),
83	        onupdate=utcnow,
84	    )
85	
86	
87	def tenant_fk(target_table: str, local_column: str | None = None) -> sa.ForeignKeyConstraint:
88	    """Tenant-safe foreign key for __table_args__ (D-007 item 4).
89	
90	    - tenant_fk("adm_tenants") anchors tenant_id itself to the tenants root;
91	      every tenant-scoped table carries this backstop.
92	    - tenant_fk("inv_items", "item_id") builds the composite (tenant_id, item_id)
93	      -> (inv_items.tenant_id, inv_items.id) FK, so a child row can never point
94	      at a parent row of another tenant; the parent declares tenant_unique().
95	    """
96	    if local_column is None:
97	        return sa.ForeignKeyConstraint(["tenant_id"], [f"{target_table}.id"])
98	    return sa.ForeignKeyConstraint(
99	        ["tenant_id", local_column],
100	        [f"{target_table}.tenant_id", f"{target_table}.id"],
101	    )
102	
103	
104	def tenant_unique() -> sa.UniqueConstraint:
105	    """UNIQUE (tenant_id, id) — required on every tenant-scoped table that is
106	    referenced through tenant_fk() composite FKs (D-007 item 4). Any OTHER unique
107	    constraint starting with tenant_id needs an explicit name at the call site:
108	    the D-022 naming convention keys on column 0 only and would collide."""
109	    return sa.UniqueConstraint("tenant_id", "id")

112	class User(UuidPKMixin, TenantMixin, AuditMixin, TimestampMixin, Base):
113	    """Auth principal (D-008). Cross-cutting platform entity, so it lives in core
114	    (STRUCTURE §2 litmus: users are not a business concept). Provisioning is owned
115	    by modules/admin (PLAN 14); login lookup runs under system_context (D-007 site 1).
116	    HR compensation/PII masking is HR's concern later — these rows are credentials only.
117	    Audited (D-010): security-relevant; password_hash is excluded from every diff."""

119	    __tablename__ = "core_users"

121	    __audit_exclude__ = frozenset({"password_hash"})
122	    __table_args__ = (

124	        # would collide with tenant_unique() below.
125	        sa.UniqueConstraint("tenant_id", "email", name="uq_core_users_tenant_id_email"),
126	        tenant_unique(),
127	        tenant_fk("adm_tenants"),
128	    )

132	    full_name: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(sa.String(200), nullable=True)

65	async def collection_etag(
66	    session: AsyncSession,
67	    model: type,
68	    *extra_filters: sa.ColumnElement[bool],
69	    request_fingerprint: str = "",
70	) -> str:
71	    """Compute a WEAK collection validator from ONE cheap aggregate query (D-035).
72	
73	    ``SELECT COUNT(model.id), MAX(model.updated_at)`` — tenant-scoped automatically by the D-007
74	    ``do_orm_execute`` listener (the aggregate references the model's mapped columns, so the
75	    tenant predicate is injected). ``extra_filters`` narrow the collection to the same rows the
76	    list endpoint returns (e.g. a ``fiscal_year_id`` filter), so the validator tracks the visible
77	    slice, not the whole table. ``request_fingerprint`` (cursor+limit+filters of the actual
78	    request) is folded into the returned tag so a 304 can never serve a different page slice.
79	
80	    The returned string is the full weak ETag ready for the ``ETag`` header / ``If-None-Match``
81	    comparison: ``W/"<count>-<max_micros>-<tenant8>-<reqfingerprint>"``.
82	    """
83	    stmt = sa.select(sa.func.count(model.id), sa.func.max(model.updated_at))
84	    for clause in extra_filters:
85	        stmt = stmt.where(clause)
86	    count, max_updated = (await session.execute(stmt)).one()
87	
88	    # Microsecond epoch keeps the component compact and monotonic; empty collection → "" so the
89	    # validator is stable for an empty set yet flips the moment the first row lands (count 0->1).
90	    max_component = (
91	        "" if max_updated is None else str(int(max_updated.timestamp() * 1_000_000))
92	    )
93	    return f'W/"{count}-{max_component}-{_tenant_component()}-{request_fingerprint}"'

96	def _normalize_tag(raw: str) -> str:
97	    """Strip a leading weak marker so weak/strong forms of the same tag compare equal. Per RFC
98	    7232 the weak-comparison function ignores the ``W/`` prefix; our validators are always weak,
99	    but a client may echo the value with or without it, so normalize both sides."""
100	    raw = raw.strip()
101	    if raw.startswith("W/"):
102	        raw = raw[2:]
103	    return raw

106	def check_not_modified(request: Request, etag: str) -> bool:
107	    """True when the client's ``If-None-Match`` satisfies ``etag`` (RFC 7232 weak comparison).
108	
109	    Handles the ``*`` value (matches any existing representation → 304 whenever the resource
110	    exists) and a comma-separated list of candidate tags. Comparison is weak: the ``W/`` prefix is
111	    ignored on both sides. A missing/blank header → False (the endpoint then serves a normal 200).
112	    """
113	    header = request.headers.get("if-none-match")
114	    if not header:
115	        return False
116	    candidates = [part.strip() for part in header.split(",") if part.strip()]
117	    if "*" in candidates:
118	        return True
119	    target = _normalize_tag(etag)
120	    return any(_normalize_tag(candidate) == target for candidate in candidates)

123	async def conditional_response[T](
124	    request: Request,
125	    response: Response,
126	    etag: str,
127	    builder: Callable[[], Awaitable[T]],
128	) -> T | Response:
129	    """Conditional-GET epilogue for a reference list endpoint (D-035).
130	
131	    Given the already-computed collection ``etag``: if the client's ``If-None-Match`` matches,
132	    return a bare ``304`` carrying ONLY the ``ETag`` header and NO body — and crucially WITHOUT
133	    awaiting ``builder``, so the expensive full-page query never runs on the 304 path (this is what
134	    makes a conditional request cheaper than the unconditional one). Otherwise set the ``ETag``
135	    header on the real response and return ``await builder()`` (the ``Page`` payload).
136	
137	    Returning a starlette ``Response`` directly bypasses the route's ``response_model``, so FastAPI
138	    does not try to validate the empty 304 body against ``Page[T]`` (verified by a test).
139	    """
140	    if check_not_modified(request, etag):

196	async def paginate[T](
197	    session: AsyncSession,
198	    stmt: Select[tuple[T]],
199	    *,
200	    order_by: list[OrderKey],
201	    pk: InstrumentedAttribute[Any],
202	    cursor: str | None = None,
203	    limit: int = DEFAULT_LIMIT,
204	    filters: str = "",
205	) -> Page[T]:
206	    """Keyset-paginate ``stmt`` and return a ``Page[T]`` (D-014). ``order_by`` is the whitelisted
207	    business sort; ``pk`` (the model's id) is appended as the mandatory unique tiebreaker so the
208	    cursor is stable. ``filters`` is the router's filter fingerprint (see
209	    :func:`filter_fingerprint`) baked into the cursor. The single generic helper module routers
210	    use — they never hand-roll keyset SQL.
211	
212	    Fetches ``limit + 1`` rows; if the extra row arrives, the page is full and ``next_cursor`` is
213	    minted from the LAST returned row's sort-key tuple. The cursor (when present) is decoded and
214	    validated against this request's sort + filter fingerprint, then turned into the expanded-OR
215	    seek predicate that selects strictly-after rows."""
216	    if limit < 1:
217	        limit = 1
218	    keys = [*order_by, OrderKey(pk, SortDirection.ASC)]
219	    sort_spec = _sort_spec(keys)
220	
221	    seek_stmt = stmt
222	    if cursor is not None:
223	        key_values = decode_cursor(cursor, sort_spec, filters)
224	        if len(key_values) != len(keys):
225	            raise _invalid_cursor()
226	        seek_stmt = seek_stmt.where(_seek_predicate(keys, key_values))
227	
228	    seek_stmt = _apply_order(seek_stmt, keys).limit(limit + 1)
229	    rows = list((await session.execute(seek_stmt)).scalars().all())
230	
231	    has_more = len(rows) > limit
232	    items = rows[:limit]
233	    next_cursor: str | None = None
234	    if has_more and items:
235	        last = items[-1]
236	        next_cursor = encode_cursor(
237	            [getattr(last, key.name) for key in keys], sort_spec, filters
238	        )
239	    return Page(items=items, next_cursor=next_cursor, limit=limit)

245	    hand-rolled (and the envelope can't drift between endpoints)."""
246	    return Page(

=== PARITY Inventory ===
5:**Methodology.** All twelve functional areas below were verified through live web research against current sources (SAP Help Portal, SAP Learning, SAP Community, SAP PRESS, and ERP consulting publications); no area was built from the embedded knowledge baseline alone. Five areas — Financial Accounting, Inventory Management & Warehousing, Quality Management & Plant Maintenance, Project System, and Cross-cutting platform concepts — supplemented web findings with embedded S/4HANA knowledge for specific subtopics or where source pages could not be fetched; these are flagged in the Sources appendix.
28:| Inventory Management & Warehousing (MM-IM / EWM) | 5 | 3 | 3 | 11 |
64:In current S/4HANA, Controlling is no longer a separate ledger world: FI and CO are merged into the Universal Journal (ACDOCA), so every posting carries cost center, profit center, project/WBS, order, and profitability-segment dimensions, and all CO reporting is a real-time projection of that single table; cost elements have become G/L accounts. The practitioner-essential core comprises cost center accounting, profit center accounting, internal orders (deprecated in S/4HANA Cloud in favor of project cost collectors), product cost planning and cost object controlling, Margin Analysis (account-based CO-PA), universal allocations, activity types with internal activity allocation, and cost center planning/budgeting, with Material Ledger actual costing as an optional deepening. Atlas v1's design matches the architectural core and S/4HANA Cloud's direction (including replacing internal orders with projects), but leaves activity-rate machinery, planning/budgeting, variance decomposition, and multi-dimensional margin segments for later.
72:| **Product cost planning (standard cost estimates)** | Partial | manufacturing | Atlas plans manufacturing-fed product costing (actual costs, WIP, finish-to-stock valuation) but does not state a BOM/routing cost-rollup engine, cost component split, or standard price release/costing-run machinery. Later: Add a cost-rollup service over BOM/routing data that produces standard costs with a component split, used to value finished-goods receipts and compute variances. |
73:| **Cost object controlling (WIP, variances, settlement)** | Partial | manufacturing | Atlas plans the core flow — WIP journals and finish-to-stock postings, which matches S/4HANA's modern event-based direction — but variance decomposition (input price/quantity, resource usage, lot size), scrap analysis, and settlement profiles are not planned. Later: Add variance categorization computed from journal deltas at order close, posting categorized variance lines to the ledger and the margin report. |
78:| Material Ledger / actual costing | Out of scope | — | Not mentioned in the Atlas plan; actual costing is an optional deepening in S/4HANA (mandatory only as the multi-currency valuation substructure), so omitting it from v1 is a defensible cut. Later: Add a periodic actual-cost roll-up job that recomputes inventory and COGS values from accumulated journal lines and posts revaluation entries. |
93:| **Goods receipt against purchase order** | Full | inventory | Later: Atlas plans GR in the v1 chain; stock/valuation postings are owned by the inventory module. |
103:## Inventory Management & Warehousing (MM-IM / EWM)
105:In current S/4HANA (2025), MM-IM covers the material/product master, all goods movements recorded in the unified MATDOC table, stock types and special stocks, physical inventory with cycle counting, and material valuation through the now-mandatory Material Ledger (standard price, moving average, FIFO/balance-sheet valuation), plus batch and serial number management and reorder-point replenishment. Warehousing is handled by embedded or decentralized EWM, whose basic tier covers storage-type/bin structures, putaway and stock-removal strategies, and handling units, while waves, slotting, labor management and MFS sit in the advanced (separately licensed) tier. Atlas v1 covers the transactional inventory core well (moves as single source of truth, MAV+FIFO costing, counts, lot/serial, reorder points) but deliberately stops short of stock-status/special-stock dimensions, standard costing, and the EWM execution layer.
109:| **Material / product master with item types and multi-UoM** | Full | inventory | Later: Richer attribute views (classification, plant-specific MRP data) can be layered onto the item entity later. |
110:| **Goods movements with movement types (GR, GI, transfer posting, stock transfer)** | Full | inventory | — |
111:| **Stock types and special stocks (unrestricted / QI / blocked; consignment, subcontracting, in-transit)** | Partial | inventory | Atlas v1 tracks quantity per warehouse/bin via stock moves but plans no stock-status dimension (QI/blocked) and no special-stock ownership categories such as consignment or subcontractor stock. Later: Add status and ownership dimensions to stock quants/move lines, with status-change moves reusing the existing move ledger. |
112:| **Physical inventory and cycle counting with difference posting** | Full | inventory | Later: Sampling-based inventory and ABC-driven count scheduling can be added on top of the count engine later. |
113:| **Material valuation: moving average, standard price, FIFO (Material Ledger)** | Partial | inventory | Atlas v1 plans moving average AND FIFO per item category with event-driven COGS posting, but omits standard costing with variance (price-difference) postings, which manufacturers treat as essential. Later: Add a standard-cost method to the per-item-category costing engine, posting purchase/production variances to dedicated variance accounts. |
114:| **Batch (lot) and serial number management** | Full | inventory | Later: Automatic batch determination (FEFO, characteristics-based selection) and shelf-life blocking can be added as picking-time rules later. |
115:| **Reorder point / consumption-based replenishment planning** | Full | inventory | Later: Full MRP (time-phased, BOM-driven) belongs to a later manufacturing module; v1 reorder-point-to-draft-requisition covers the inventory-side core. |
116:| **Warehouse structure: warehouses, storage types/sections, storage bins and quants** | Partial | inventory | Atlas v1 plans multi-warehouse and multi-bin stock keeping, but only a flat warehouse-to-bin model: no storage-type/section hierarchy, capacity checks, or activity areas. Later: Introduce an optional storage-type/zone layer and capacity attributes on bins without changing the move ledger. |
159:| Repetitive manufacturing (REM) | Out of scope | — | Atlas v1 supports only discrete production orders; period/rate-based order-less execution and product cost collectors are not planned. Later: Add run-schedule headers on production versions with backflush postings reusing BOM/routing and inventory movement logic. |
167:In current S/4HANA (2025/2026), QM covers quality planning (inspection plans, master inspection characteristics, sampling), quality inspection (inspection lots auto-created at goods receipt, in production, and at delivery), characteristic-level results recording, coded usage decisions that drive stock postings out of quality-inspection stock, and quality notifications/CAPA, plus certificates and supplier quality. PM-EAM centers on technical objects (equipment installed on hierarchical functional locations), maintenance notifications feeding corrective maintenance orders with a phase-based lifecycle, preventive maintenance plans (time-, performance/counter-, and strategy-based) scheduled against task lists, and measurement points/counters for condition readings. Against the Atlas v1 plan, the GR-inspection-to-disposition flow, equipment register, and corrective/interval-based preventive orders cover a credible minimal core, but inspection plans, results recording, quality and maintenance notifications, functional locations, and measurement points are genuine gaps practitioners will notice.
171:| **Inspection lots** | Partial | quality | Only GR-origin lots via an inspection flag are planned; production/in-process, delivery, and manual lot origins plus sampling/sample-size logic are not. Later: Extend the existing lot object with additional origins (production order, delivery, manual) and sampling procedures. |
172:| **Inspection plans and master inspection characteristics** | Out of scope | — | Explicitly excluded from the v1 list; v1 lots are plan-less binary accept/reject with no characteristic or sampling master data. Later: Introduce inspection plan + characteristic master data and assign plans to lots at creation. |
173:| **Results recording** | Out of scope | — | Depends on inspection plans/characteristics, which are cut; v1 captures only a lot-level accept/reject outcome, not measured values. Later: After plans/characteristics exist, add a characteristic-level results entry screen with auto-valuation. |
175:| **Quality notifications (defects/complaints/CAPA)** | Out of scope | — | No defect/complaint workflow in v1; a rejected lot only moves stock and does not open a tracked quality issue. Later: Add a generic notification/issue object (shared with maintenance notifications) linkable to lots, suppliers, and materials. |
195:| **Time recording with account assignment (CATS-style timesheet)** | Full | hr | Later: Planned core (capture + project/cost-center allocation) matches CATS; approval/transfer-to-costing flows can be hardened later. |
209:S/4HANA Project System manages internal, capital-investment, and customer projects through hierarchical work breakdown structures (WBS) and optional networks/activities, covering structure planning, scheduling, cost and revenue planning, budgeting with availability control, execution postings (time via CATS, procurement, goods movements), and period-end close via settlement and results analysis / event-based revenue recognition. In current S/4HANA (2025/2026) the area spans classic PS (on-premise/private cloud) and the Fiori-based Enterprise Projects and Professional Services Projects in Enterprise Portfolio and Project Management (public cloud). The Atlas v1 plan (WBS as costing objects, time and purchases postable to WBS, a project cost report) covers the execution-side core — structures and actual-cost collection — but deliberately omits the planning and financial-close layers: networks/scheduling, cost planning, budgeting/availability control, settlement, results analysis/revenue recognition, and customer-project billing are all out of scope for v1.
219:| **Procurement and expense postings to projects** | Partial | projects | Atlas v1 plans actual purchase and expense postings to WBS, but PR/PO commitment tracking and project stock / project MRP are not planned. Later: Derive commitment records from open purchase orders assigned to WBS, then add project-stock segments in inventory. |

=== PLAN 5 ===
64:## Phase 5 — Inventory & Warehouse
66:- [ ] 5.1 Items (stocked/non-stocked/service), item categories, multi-UoM with conversions, lot & serial masters
67:- [ ] 5.2 Warehouses + bins; stock moves as single source of truth; on-hand/availability projections

127:- [ ] 15.2 Design system: DataGrid, FormBuilder, Kanban, KpiCard, DocFlowViewer (ERP-agnostic, tested)
130:- [ ] 15.5 Inventory UIs (items, stock overview, moves, counts)

3	Over the wire: first GET returns 200 + ETag; an immediate If-None-Match re-GET returns 304 with the
4	same ETag and an empty body; creating a row in that collection invalidates the prior ETag (200, new
5	tag); a write to a DIFFERENT tenant's same collection does NOT invalidate this tenant's ETag; a
6	different page (cursor/limit) carries a DIFFERENT ETag so a 304 can never serve the wrong slice; the
7	304 path is cheaper than the 200 path (it skips the page query); the ``*`` wildcard yields 304; and

permission keys, registered into the core RBAC catalog at import (D-009).

Started as a SINGLE file (STRUCTURE §8.4: split into a constants/ package only at the 400-line
cap, the finance precedent); it sits well under that for PLAN 5.1.

Item codes are USER-SUPPLIED and unique per tenant (the ``UNIQUE(tenant_id, item_code)`` on
inv_items) — mirroring how chart-of-accounts codes work (Account.code is required on create, not
auto-numbered). So inventory declares NO number sequence here: masters carry no gapless document
number (those are for journal entries / orders / receipts in D-012). When stock *moves* land in
PLAN 5.2 they register documents and claim numbers; the item master itself does not.
"""

from enum import StrEnum

from app.core.rbac import register_permissions


class ItemType(StrEnum):
    """What an item IS, which decides whether it carries stock (D-020).

    - STOCKED: a physical good tracked in inventory — the only type that participates in stock
      moves, costing and lot/serial tracking.
    - NON_STOCKED: a purchasable/sellable good NOT held in inventory (e.g. drop-ship, expensed
      supplies) — no on-hand quantity, no costing layer.
    - SERVICE: a non-physical line item (labour, fees) — never stocked, never tracked.

    The service rejects tracking/costing participation for NON_STOCKED/SERVICE so the invariant
    "only STOCKED items have stock" holds from the masters up (validated again when moves land)."""

    STOCKED = "STOCKED"
    NON_STOCKED = "NON_STOCKED"
    SERVICE = "SERVICE"


class CostingMethod(StrEnum):
    """How a stocked item is valued (D-020). Defaulted onto the item FROM its category at create
    but STORED on the item, because D-020 changes it only while no stock exists and the item is
    the costing unit. The moving-average valuation table and FIFO cost layers arrive in PLAN 5.3;
    5.1 only records the method so receipts know which engine to use."""

    MOVING_AVERAGE = "MOVING_AVERAGE"
    FIFO = "FIFO"


class TrackingMode(StrEnum):
    """Whether a stocked item's units are individually identified (parity: batch/serial mgmt).

    - NONE: fungible — quantity only (the default).
    - LOT: grouped by lot/batch code; one lot row per received batch (inv_lots), created at
      receipt (5.2+).
    - SERIAL: each unit uniquely identified; one inv_serials row per unit, created at receipt.

    Tracking is PER ITEM and only meaningful for STOCKED items — the service forbids a non-NONE
    mode on NON_STOCKED/SERVICE items."""

    NONE = "NONE"
    LOT = "LOT"
    SERIAL = "SERIAL"


class LotStatus(StrEnum):
    """Lifecycle of a lot/batch instance (parity: batch management). For 5.1 the table merely
    EXISTS — lots are created during receipts (5.2+); AVAILABLE is the default a receipt sets,
    the others are reached by later quality/expiry flows. No dead CRUD now (masters-only)."""

    AVAILABLE = "AVAILABLE"
    BLOCKED = "BLOCKED"
    CONSUMED = "CONSUMED"


class SerialStatus(StrEnum):

    table exists for 5.1 and is populated at receipt (5.2+): IN_STOCK on receipt, ISSUED when
    the unit leaves, BLOCKED by quality holds."""
